Rumors suggest Apple will launch a brand-new MacBook Ultra this autumn as part of its expanding "Ultra" product line. Here are six new features the MacBook Ultra is expected to bring.

#1: All-new design, thinner and lighter than the MacBook Pro

According to Bloomberg, Apple's new MacBook model is a "complete redesign" that is thinner and lighter than the current MacBook Pro.

The MacBook Ultra was originally expected to launch under the "MacBook Pro" branding but with an all-new design. While that approach is still possible, current rumours point to the "Ultra" branding.

We don't yet know whether the ports will be reduced compared to the MacBook Pro, but that's a possibility. However, I'd be surprised if Apple pushed the "thin and light" direction too far, since the MacBook Ultra is likely to attract a lot of Pro users.

#2: M5 Pro and M5 Max chips

The new M6 chip series has long been expected to debut on the MacBook Ultra, but recent rumours tell a different story.

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports that Apple has shelved plans for the M6 Pro and M6 Max chips, and is instead accelerating development of a high-performance M7 chip.

So while a future MacBook Ultra will feature an M7 chip, this year's model is reportedly sticking with the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips currently used in the MacBook Pro.

#3: Touchscreen — a first for Mac

Touch support is coming to the Mac, and the MacBook Ultra will be the first model to feature a touchscreen.

According to Mark Gurman, Apple is adding touch to the Mac as a supplementary input method, not as a replacement for the keyboard and trackpad.

macOS Golden Gate will come with a number of optimisations, offering a control interface better suited to touch operation, while remaining equally usable for those without a touchscreen.

#4: OLED display

Every iPhone now features an OLED display, and the iPad Pro joined the party with its excellent tandem OLED in 2024. But the Mac has always been the exception — until now.

The MacBook Ultra will adopt OLED, becoming the first Mac to feature this display technology.

OLED delivers purer blacks, better contrast, and wider viewing angles, and is also expected to bring longer battery life to the MacBook Ultra.

#5: Dynamic Island

The 2021 MacBook Pro was the first Mac to feature a notch, but the MacBook Ultra is set to drop that design.

The new MacBook Ultra is expected to switch to a hole-punch camera cutout and introduce a new software feature: Dynamic Island.

Just like on the iPhone, Dynamic Island not only uses software to mask the camera cutout, but also brings new practical functionality to macOS — including serving as the home of Siri AI.

Variable #6: Cellular option with C2 modem

Apple has yet to release a Mac with cellular connectivity, but rumours suggest that could soon change.

Of course, there's no guarantee Macs will get cellular this year, but with Apple's C2 modem set to debut this autumn alongside the iPhone 18 Pro, the timing seems just right.

Which new feature of the MacBook Ultra are you most looking forward to? Let us know in the comments.
